prayerExcerpt.en-US: Admit us, we beseech you, into their company, not weighing our merits, but granting us your pardon.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Concedei, não por nossos méritos, mas por vossa bondade, o convívio dos Apóstolos e Mártires.

meta.face: A young woman of about twenty-five with a fair, narrow, diamond-shaped face — high cheekbones, a slim nose with a slightly upturned tip, wide-set grey eyes under fine, straight light brows, a narrow pointed chin and a small, full mouth; light auburn hair braided and coiled at the nape under a pearl fillet (not loose, no veil), and a composed, compassionate gaze.
meta.basis: Carpaccio's St. Anastasia in the Zadar polyptych, where her relics are kept: light auburn hair under a pearled fillet, a green gown, a dark mantle and a palm; the Orthodox icon gives the phial of the Pharmakolytria. Braiding the hair is an artistic choice to keep her apart from the long-haired virgin martyrs.
meta.excerpt: content/of/order/order-of-mass.json, Roman Canon (Eucharistic Prayer I), Nobis quoque, which names 'Agnes, Cecilia, Anastasia' (en-US lines 198-201, pt-BR lines 190-192)
